text: The lines stand on the wrapper as on the title page (frame 007): the faculty in two underlined lines at the top right, then «No. 2» in Latin type, the title, the author, a short rule, the line on the editors, the two editors in two columns (Mušarrafa on the right, Aḥmad on the left, «و» between them), a double rule and the printer with the year. The wrapper prints أحمد with the hamza, the title page احمد without it.
The faculty stands at the top right in two underlined lines; under the title, a short rule; the two editors in two columns with «و» between them; a double rule above the printer and the year.
The facsimile is reproduced as an image; its handwritten text is not transcribed.

Frame 026: 19 Muharram 743 is 23 June 1342 (Julian), a Sunday, by the arithmetical calendar counted from 15 July 622, and 24 June, a Monday, from 16 July 622; the Sunday of the colophon agrees with the first.
The verso of the facsimile plate (frame 009), blank.

The preface (frames 011-012) states that the manuscript the edition follows is a copy made about five hundred years after the author's death, that the notes in its margins, added by readers, are not treated as part of the text, and that the editors corrected what they judged obvious copying errors without marking the corrections. The edition is therefore not a diplomatic edition of the manuscript; this transcription follows the edition as printed. The preface is dated 26/9/1937.
The verso of the last page of the editors' study (frame 026), blank; the facsimile of frame 028 faces the first page of the text.
The facsimile is reproduced as an image; its handwritten text is not transcribed. Its lines correspond to the edition's text of frames 029-030.

L01: the basmala is set as a centred heading in a large display type; the word الله is printed as the usual ligature with shadda and a small alif above, which the edition's font draws from the plain letters.
L02-L03: both lines are printed with a paragraph indent.
The final yā' is printed without dots throughout this page (الخوارزمى, التى, على, فى, الهدى, النبى, ويبقى, أبقى, شجعنى); the print's dotless form is kept.

Set without a word space after a non-connecting letter, and transcribed so: مماكانوا (L12), مالم (L14), ماكان (L20; but ما كان later on the same line, and on L15). In وأكرمه (L18) the gap after the alif is a letter gap within the word.

Without tanwīn as printed: وتذللا, وخشوعا (L05), خللا (L16); with tanwīn on the final alif: اقراراً (L04), محمداً (L05), نظراً, واحتساباً (L10), مستخرجاً (L14), مستغلقاً (L15), مستبهماً, مستوعراً (L20).
Plain alif where a hamza might be expected, as printed: افتتحه (L02), افترض (L03), الامام (L18), وادنائهم (L19).
L14-L15: شرح مما أبقى / الأولون, as printed.
Set without a word space after a non-connecting letter, and transcribed so: مااستودعوا (L05), إنماتركبت (L08); after the tā' marbūṭa: العشرةوتثلث (L10).
Plain alif where a hamza might be expected, as printed: الانبياء and اليه (L07, where L02 has إليه), الى (L11, where L10, L12 and L13 have إلى).
Without tanwīn as printed: مقدما, وراجيا (L04); with tanwīn on the final alif: كتاباً, مختصراً, حاصراً (L01), عدداً (L08).
The final yā' is printed without dots (فى, وكرى, تعالى, وإنى, التى, تثنى, وهى).
L06: وبالله توفيق فى هذا, as printed: توفيق without the yā' of the first person.
L07: اجذاره is printed with a plain alif, where L08 has أجذاره.

L12 is set tight to fill the measure. Without a word space after a non-connecting letter, and transcribed so: بماعادلهامن, مايرد; after a connecting letter, whose final form marks the end of the word, a word space is transcribed although the print sets the words close: إلى مال, اليه المال. The full stop at the end of L12 is set close.
L01: شىء with a dotless yā' before the hamza.
Without tanwīn as printed: بعضا (L05); with tanwīn on the final alif: جذوراً, عدداً (L05), عدداً (L06), جذراً (L09).

Plain alif where a hamza might be expected, as printed: الاموال (L01, L10; but الأموال on L04, L12 and أموال on L02, L11), اربعة اجذار (L07), اربعمائة (L09), اجناس (L11), اجذاره (L13, L14), اذا (L13).

Set without a word space after a tā' marbūṭa, and transcribed so: ثلاثةوكقولك, خمسةأموال (L02), ستةوكذلك (L03), عشرةاجذاره (L14). After a connecting letter, whose final form marks the end of the word, a word space is transcribed even where the print sets the words close: نصف مال (L03), يكون منه (L07, L08, L09), ومعناه أى (L13).
L09: the full stop follows the note mark (١) without a space.
Without tanwīn as printed: مالا (L05), عددا (L06, L11), أموالا (L12), درهما (L13); with tanwīn on the final alif: تاماً (L05), جذوراً (L11).
L01, L08: المسئلة, the hamza on a seat of yā', as printed.
L13: ثلثة, spelled without the alif, as printed (L03 has ثلاثة).
Set without a word space after a non-connecting letter, and transcribed so: وهوجذر (L03; but وهو جذر on L13), أوأقل (L04), أربعةوعشرين (L09), اربعةوعشرين (L10). L04 has ما كان with a space.

Plain alif where a hamza might be expected, as printed: اربعة (L02), الاجذار (L03, L17), فاردده, واردد (L04), اجذار (L06, L07, L09, L17), واربعين (L06, L07), احدهما (L07), فاردد (L08), اجذاره (L10, L15), اربعةوعشرين (L10); with the hamza: أربعةوعشرين (L09), أجذاره (L14).
Without tanwīn as printed: درهما (L06, L07, L09, L12, L14, L15, L17), جمعا (L06), مالا (L08, L16, L17), ونصفا (L11), وربعا (L11, L12); with tanwīn on the final alif: تاماً (L16).
L16: كلما, printed as one word.
L05: وأحد, with a hamza on the alif, as printed, in مال وأحد وعشرون (one square and twenty-one); L06 has واحدا وعشرين.
L08: فأنقص with a hamza on the alif, as printed; L02 and L09 have فانقص, فانقصه.

Set without a word space after a non-connecting letter, and transcribed so: عادلهامن (L04), والعددالتى (L05), جذرهاوهو (L09). After a connecting letter, whose final form marks the end of the word, a word space is transcribed where the print sets the words close: ان شاء (L04), قولك مال, وعشرون من (L05), أى مال (L06), والعشرين التى (L08).
L02: the note mark (١) stands after وهو, close before خمسة; L07: the note mark (٢) stands close before أن. The full stops after الله (L04) and المال (L07) are set close.

Plain alif where a hamza might be expected, as printed: احدا (L02), الاجذار (L02, L07, L09, L11, L15), ان (L04), اجذاره (L06), انها, اربعة (L09), وان (L10), واربعون, فاذا, الى (L12), فان (L13), الابواب (L14), انك, اذا (L15).
Without tanwīn as printed: احدا (L02), واحدا, درهما (L06), جميعا (L14).
L05, L11: ثلثة, spelled without the alif, as printed (L12 has الثلاثة).

Set without a word space after a non-connecting letter, and transcribed so: وأربعةمن (L05), ستةوربعا, جذرهاوهو (L07), وهوجذر (L08), ماكان (L09). After a connecting letter, whose final form marks the end of the word, a word space is transcribed where the print sets the words close: فتكون اربعة (L08), أتيت على (L10). L08: in واحد ونصف the د and the و stand 38 px apart (nearest approach of the letters, at 400 ppi), as far as the other word spaces of the line, and a space is transcribed; in وهوجذر the و and the ج stand 28 px apart, as in وهوجذر on frame 33 (L03, 26 px), where the same words set with a space (frame 33, L13) stand 46 px apart. L03: in لا زيادة the ا and the ز stand 24 px apart; without a word space the same letters stand 11 to 14 px apart (مازدنا, frame 037; أردنا, frame 043), and a space is transcribed.
Plain alif where a hamza might be expected, as printed: الاجذار (L02), الى (L03; L09 and L12 have إلى), الاول (L04), اجذار (L05), الاربعة (L07), اربعة (L08), اكثر (L09; L03 has أكثر).
Without tanwīn as printed: مالا, واحدا, ونصفا (L06), وربعا (L07), درهما (L15).
L01: the note mark (١) ends the line, after مستحيلة; L09 ends without a full stop, as printed.

The figure: a square divided into nine. The middle square is marked المال, with a letter at two of its opposite corners; the rectangles on its sides are marked ح (above), ج (left), ك (right) and ط (below); each corner square is marked ستة وربع; a letter stands outside the upper left corner of the whole and ه outside its lower right. The figure is drawn, not set in type, and is reproduced as an image.

Letters printed as the labels of the figure carry a short wavy line above them (here a line above): اب (L02, L11, L13, L20), the line over its ب; ده (L20, L22), the line over its ه; ط and ك (L13). The first and the last of the four labels of L13, ع and ح, are printed without it; the last has the initial form of the letter, without a dot.

L13: the four labels after سطوح are printed ع, ط, ك, ح. The first has the shape of an ʿayn (a closed head and a tail, without a dot), unlike the ح of the figure; the figure has no ع. The same sort names a point thirteen times on frame 38. See the critical note AK01-CN001.

Set without a word space after a non-connecting letter, and transcribed so: وهواثنان (L07), الخمسةوالعشرين and زواياسطح (L19), الثمانيةمثل (L21). After a connecting letter, whose final form marks the end of the word, a word space is transcribed where the print sets the words close: المال الذى and تعرفه وتعرف (L01), إن مع and مع المال (L06), على زواياسطح (L19).

Plain alif where a hamza might be expected, as printed: الاضلاع (L01, L14), اضلاعه (L02; the same line has أضلاعه), اعداد (L04; L03 has الأعداد), اجذاره (L06), اخذنا (L07), اضلاع (L09), اربعة (L11, L20), اربع (L16), اجذار (L18), فاذا (L19, L21), الاربع (L19; L14 has الأربع), الاعظم (L20; L22 has الأعظم).
The print stretches some words with the elongation stroke (kashīda) to fill the line, as جذر and وعرضه (L13), أيضا (L14), فصار (L15); the stroke is not transcribed.

L02: between the second ضلع and the following word, a small vertical string of ink specks stands at the height of the letters: a blemish of the print, neither a letter nor a note mark; not transcribed.
L18: the full stop at the end of the line is set close to العدد. L22 ends without a full stop; the sentence runs on to the next page.
The ب of the label اب is printed without its dot every time (L02, L11, L13, L20); transcribed ٮ, the dotless form. The figure's ب has no dot either.

The figure: a square divided by two lines into four. The upper right square is marked المال, with ا at its upper right corner and ب at its lower left corner, the corner it shares with the other three; the upper left rectangle is marked ح; the lower right rectangle carries a mark shaped like a question mark, perhaps a ج; the lower left square is marked ٢٥. د stands outside the upper left corner of the whole and ه outside its lower right corner. The figure is drawn, not set in type, and is reproduced as an image.

Letters printed as the labels of the figure carry a short wavy line above them: اب (L06, L08, L09, L10, L18), the line over its ب; ده (L14), the line over its د, where frame 36 has it over the ه; ح (L08), the line over the left half of the letter and the space after it.

L08: the two labels after سطحا are ح and a ج printed upside down: the sort is turned through 180 degrees, so that the bowl of the letter opens to the left, the stroke that tops a ج runs along its foot, and the dot stands inside the bowl. Transcribed {inv:ج} and set upside down in the PDF. See the critical note AK01-CN002.

L20: the statement of the fifth case, from وأما to اجذاره, is printed in a bold face; the rest of the line, from فا نانجعل, in the face of the text. The line is printed with a paragraph indent. In the bold face the joined د and ذ come close to the shape of ر and ز; the letter after the ج of اجذاره reaches as deep below the line as the joined د of وأحد, not as deep as the joined ر of وعشرون, and is read ذ.

Set without a word space after a non-connecting letter, and transcribed so: مازدنا (L17; the ا and the ز stand 11 px apart, nearest approach of the letters at 400 ppi, where إذا زدت on frame 041, L02, sets them 32 px apart). In the bold face of L20 the word spaces are narrow: the ل of مال and the و of وأحد stand 8 px apart; the د of وأحد and the و of وعشرون stand 12 px apart, which does not show whether a space is set, and the space is written: وأحد وعشرون. After a connecting letter, whose final form marks the end of the word, a word space is transcribed where the print sets the words close: أن نزيد and فصارت خمسة (L07), طول كل (L08), سطح ده (L14), مال وأحد, تعدل عشرة, نجعل المال and المال سطحاً (L20).
Plain alif where a hamza might be expected, as printed: الاجذار (L01, L04, L09; L10 has الأجذار), الى (L06, L12), فاذا (L16), اجذاره (L20; L07 has أجذاره).
With tanwīn on the final alif: سطحاً (L20); without tanwīn as printed: أيضا (L06).
The print stretches some words with the elongation stroke (kashīda) to fill the line, as تمام (L12), فأخذنا (L15), عليه (L17); the stroke is not transcribed.
L01: the full stop after المال stands between spaces; L05 ends with a full stop set apart; L19, at the end of the narrow column, ends without one.
L20: the note mark (١) is set close after اجذاره, with a space after it.
L20: the print sets a word space inside فانا, after its first alif, and none after it: فا نانجعل (see the critical note AK01-CN005).

The ب of the label اب is printed without its dot every time (L06, L08, L09, L10, L18); transcribed ٮ, the dotless form. In L09 a small irregular speck stands 35 to 45 px below the bowl of the ب, not shaped like the printed dots.
Letters printed as the labels of the figure carry a short wavy line above them, as on frames 36 and 37 (here a line above).

The letter that names the point at which حه is halved, and the lines and surfaces that end there, is printed ع, thirteen times: نقطة ع, هع, عح (L07); عط (L08, twice; L09); حع (L09); عك, طع (L15); كع (L16); زع, عا (L21); عح (L22). It is the same sort as the first of the four labels of frame 36, L13: a closed head and a tail, without a dot. The figure of the demonstration (frame 041) has no ع, and the manuscript, in the facsimile of frame 039, writes ج. See the critical note AK01-CN003.

L02: the second letter of the label هن is a ن printed upside down: an arch open below, with the dot under its top. Transcribed {inv:ن} and set upside down in the PDF. See the critical note AK01-CN004.

Set without a word space after a non-connecting letter, and transcribed so: والزواياوهو (L10; the ا and the و stand 9 px apart, nearest approach of the letters at 400 ppi); مزمثل (L17, at the end of the line: the ز and the م 10 px apart; at the beginning of the same line the same words stand 65 px apart and are transcribed with a space). After a connecting letter, whose final form marks the end of the word, a word space is transcribed where the print sets the words close: وحدث سطح (L09), تبين لنا (L10), لك وهو (L16), سطح صغير (L20). In واحد وعشرون (L05) and الواحد والعشرون (L13) the د and the و stand 16 and 21 px apart, in L18 and L19 56 and 47 px; without a word space these letters stand 6 to 7 px apart (دونه, frame 031; الجذور, frame 043), and a space is transcribed in all four.
L09: فصار خط is set with a word space: the ر and the خ stand 27 px apart, although the tail of the ر reaches under the خ.
Plain alif where a hamza might be expected, as printed: اليه (L01), فان (L04, L22), الاضلاع (L10; L01 and L04 have الأضلاع).
With tanwīn on the final alif: مربعاً, سطحاً (L01), جميعاً (L03), مضروباً (L04), إذاً (L11); without tanwīn as printed: مزيدا (L17).
The commas of L01, L02, L03 and L05 stand between spaces; L12 has a full stop between spaces, and L21 ends with one set apart. L22 ends without punctuation; the sentence runs on to the next page.
The ب of the label هب is printed without its dot every time (L02, L13, L14, L18); transcribed ٮ, the dotless form.
The facsimile is reproduced as an image; its handwritten text is not transcribed. Its lines correspond to the edition's text from frame 038, L02, to the end of the demonstration on frame 041.

The manuscript names the point at which the line حه is halved with ج, a jīm with its dot: «على نقطة ج» and «خط هج» in the fifth line of the page, where the print has ع (frame 038, L07; critical note AK01-CN003). In the first line it writes the label هن with the ن upright (frame 038, L02; critical note AK01-CN004).
The facsimile of frame 039 shows through the paper, mirrored. A thin dark curved line near the lower left of the leaf, a hair or a fibre, is not ink of the print.

The figure of the fifth case, drawn, not set in type: a rectangle divided by three vertical lines and, in its left part, by a horizontal line, into the square on the half of the roots, with the small square inside it, and the square of the root beside the rectangle of the twenty-one; the sides of the small square are marked ٢ and those of the square of the root ٣. Its labels: م, ل and ك along the top; on the middle line ه at its left end, then ز, at the middle of the line a letter shaped like ح without a dot, ا, and ح at the right end; ن inside the lower left square; along the bottom a round ه, ط, ب and د. It has no ع (critical note AK01-CN003).

The rectangle of the figure takes in, at its top right, the line L04 «وذلك ما أردنا أن نبين», which the print sets beside the top of the figure, at the height of its upper labels; the line is transcribed as L04 and stands in the image as well.
L01: the label حع, the ح without a dot and the ع the same sort as on frame 038 (critical note AK01-CN003); L02: the label زح.

L05: the statement of the sixth case, from وأما to مالا, is printed in a bold face, with a paragraph indent; the note mark (٢) stands apart after it, and the rest of the line, from فانا, is in the face of the text. Here the print sets فانا نجعل with the space after فانا (30 px, nearest approach of the letters at 400 ppi; within فانا 15 px); on frame 037, L20, the same words have the space inside فانا.

Set without a word space after a non-connecting letter, and transcribed so: وهوسطح (L06; the و and the س stand 26 px apart, as far as the و and the ه inside وهو on the same line, 26 px; set with a space, the same words stand 46 px apart on frame 038, L10, and 43 px on frame 036, L01). After a non-connecting letter a word space is transcribed where the gap is a space: سبعة وهو (L02, 21 px, where the same letters set without a space stand 5 to 9 px apart on frames 032 to 036), واحدا وعشرين (L03, 27 px), الزوايا وهوسطح (L06, 28 px, against 9 px in والزواياوهو on frame 038, L10).
Plain alif where a hamza might be expected, as printed: فان (L01), فانا (L05); with hamza: الأول (L01), أكثر, إذا (L02), أجذاره (L03), أردنا, أن (L04), أجذار, وأربعة (L05), الأضلاع (L06, twice).
With tanwīn on the final alif: سطحاً (L05), مربعاً (L06); without tanwīn as printed: واحدا (L03), مالا (L05).
L01: the full stop after الأول stands between spaces. L04, a short line, ends without a full stop.

The editors' note (١) runs in a narrow column beside a figure of their own, a rectangle divided into squares with the dimensions ٧ and ٢, which illustrates the other solution of the fifth case; the note and its figure are the editors' work and are not reproduced. Note (٢) restates the sixth case as an equation in modern notation.

The figure, drawn, not set in type: the square of the māl, divided by two horizontal and two vertical lines; the square on the right between the two horizontal lines is marked ٢ ١/٤ (the square هط). Its labels: ب, م and ا along the top; ز on the left side and ه on the right side, at the level of the upper horizontal line; ك and ن inside, at that line; on the right side below ه, at the level of the lower horizontal line, a letter shaped like ح without a dot (the point that halves هح); ل and ط at the foot of the two inner vertical lines; د at the lower left corner and, at the lower right corner, ح in a flat form like the initial form of the letter. It has no ع. Its ب has no dot.

Letters printed as the labels of the figure carry a short wavy line above them (here a line above), over the second letter of a label of two letters. The label طل of L07 is printed without it and is transcribed without it; the same label has it in L08 and L11.

The point that halves هح, and the lines and surfaces that end there, are named with ع thirteen times: نقطة ع (L05); عط, عل (L07); اع (L08); عم, ع (L09); اع, عل, عح (L10); عم (L13); عح, اع (L20); عم (L21). It is the sort of frames 036, 038 and 041: a closed head and a tail, without a dot. See the critical note AK01-CN006. The lower right corner of the square is named with ح, in the flat form of the corner label of the figure: هح (L03, L04), عح (L10, L20).

L09: the label after خط is the single letter ع, after an empty space of 63 px (nearest approach of the letters at 400 ppi); before the label اع of L08 the space is 33 px. See the critical note AK01-CN007.

The ن of the labels is printed upside down every time on this page, as on frame 038: كن (L08), نز and من (L10), ان (L12, L16); an arch open below with the dot under its top. Transcribed {inv:ن} and set upside down in the PDF. See the critical note AK01-CN008.
The ب of the label هب (L04, L11) is printed without its dot, as in all the labels with ب on frames 036-038; transcribed ٮ, the dotless form.

In واحد ونصف (L06, L14, L19) and in the label اد before وهو (L18) the د and the و stand 21 to 25 px apart (nearest approach of the letters at 400 ppi). Without a word space these letters stand 6 to 7 px apart (دونه, frame 031; الجذور, frame 043), so the gap is a narrow word space, and a space is transcribed. Every word that ends in a non-connecting letter is followed by a space of 21 to 78 px.

L01: the word ذكرناها is set loosely to fill the line: its ذ and كر, and its كر and ناها, stand 46 and 35 px apart, as far as the word spaces of the line, while the word stands at the usual distance from its neighbours. Like the elongation strokes, these gaps stretch the line; they are not transcribed.
Plain alif where a hamza might be expected, as printed: فان (L01), الاجذار (L12, L13, L19; L01, L03, L04 and L06 have الأجذار), الاربعة (L13; L01, L04, L12 and L15 have الأربعة), فاذا (L20).
Without tanwīn as printed: سطحا, مربعا (L05).
L17: الأوله, with a final ه without dots, where المربعة on the same line has the dotted ة.
The print stretches some words with the elongation stroke (kashīda) to fill the line, as والأربعة (L01), فقطعنا (L04), فيفضل (L11), واحد (L14); the stroke is not transcribed.
L21 ends without punctuation; the sentence runs on to the next page.
L06: the chapter heading باب الضرب is printed in a bold face at the beginning of the line, followed by a wide space (94 px at 400 ppi), and the text runs on in the same line.

Notes (١) and (٢) of the editors. (١) states the principle that they take the chapter to follow: when an heir owes the estate a debt larger than his share, he keeps the whole of it, part as his share and the rest as a gift from the testator; with each son's share x, 2/3 (10 + x) = 2x, x = 5: the legatee receives five dirhams and the other son five. (٢) solves the second problem: the bequest 1/5 (10 + x) + 1, the rest 4/5 (10 + x) − 1 equal to two shares, 2x; x = 5 5/6 and the bequest 4 1/6. Both results check exactly. Notes (١) and (٢) of the editors work out the shares. (١): the wife a quarter, the mother a sixth, the rest to the brother and the two sisters, the brother 7/24 and each sister 7/48 of the estate; the heirs' part is divided into forty-eight shares, which are eight ninths of the whole, so the estate is fifty-four shares, six to the legatee.
